messages:
Anya: quick sync — we need a concrete launch checklist for the routing + econ work. customers keep asking for lower p95 and predictable cost. can we list must-have criteria vs nice-to-have? :thinking:
Sam: +1. propose must-have: p50/p95 for 1k token chat profile, cost per 1M tokens <= baseline + 15%, and no regression on quality evals (semantic-sim > 0.92). nice-to-have: dedicated cache warmup, canary by region.
Kevin: agree on structure. quick RICE take: Reach = 3 (enterprise chat customers), Impact = 4 (reduces tail latency), Confidence = 0.6, Effort = 5 dev-weeks => score ~1.44. but we should separate infra vs product effort.
Marta: for sequencing, I want: 1) routing policy defaults + quick fallbacks, 2) batch tuning and KV cache, 3) quantization profile. shipping (1) first buys immediate reliability.
Lukas: can we make the p95 target concrete? how about p95 <= 200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) and p95 <= 500ms for long ones (512 tokens)? also require 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool.
Anya: that sounds reasonable. add launch gate: no more than 5% of requests routed to fallback model under normal load. if fallback rate >5% we hold rollout.
Sam: I'll draft the launch checklist: - perf targets (p50/p95 by prompt bucket) - cost delta budget - quality regression threshold - rollout strategy (canary %, rollback criteria) - observability hooks (token-level traces). sharing in a doc in ~2h. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Automated perf run complete: baseline vs routing-econ canary: p95 short=210ms (+10%), cost delta=+12%, fallback rate=3.2% — full logs: https://internal/redwood/ci/12345
Kevin: good, numbers are close. next steps: Sam posts doc, we run one more canary with batch config B3 and KV cache enabled, then final RICE update before exec.
Marta: note from security — any private deploy customers need explicit KMS check before routing changes. tagging security for review.
Anya: thanks everyone. goal: finalize criteria + run B3 canary by end of week. if canary meets gates we proceed with staged rollout.
